answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a kernel of non-transferable work history: verified completed tasks build reputation that accrues only to one account over time. An attacker can spawn a lotus bloom of thousands of fake identities, but each begins at zero and must earn its kernel of trust individually, paying fees and waiting out the maturity period. The defender's cost stays flat while the attacker's cost rises linearly with every Sybil identity, making mass forgery unprofitable.
